confidence_notes: I based the food anchors on five web searches of cost-of-living aggregators. All of them are crowdsourced and some have few data points. MyLifeElsewhere lists an inexpensive meal at about R$39 (about US$7.46), a cappuccino at about R$10.7 (about US$2.03) and a pint of local beer at about R$12.7 (about US$2.42). Numbeo's Florianópolis ranking page lists a three-course mid-range meal for two without drinks at R$235. Expatistan lists a basic lunch menu with a drink at R$47. I converted reais to dollars at about 5.25-5.3 BRL per USD, the rate implied by the MyLifeElsewhere figures. That rate is not an official observation. I could not find a reliable aggregated price for cocktails or wine by the glass. The cocktail anchor (a standard caipirinha at a bar or restaurant, about R$28-32) and the wine-glass anchor (about R$28-30) are bounded estimates. They are set at roughly 2.3-2.5 times the beer price, a usual local ratio. One news report puts beach-club caipirinhas in Jurerê Internacional at about R$40, and upscale or beach venues can cost much more. The four accommodation anchors are general model estimates, not based on any searches or listings. They assume July, which is Florianópolis's winter low season. Summer (December-February) prices can be 1.5-2 times higher. The RBA rate came from a web search, not from reading the RBA page directly. The RBA result was published on the official exchange-rates overview page, which is the URL given. The search summary said that page listed 0.6720 USD per AUD at the 4pm fixing on 18 November 2026. A third-party site reported the same rate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Florianópolis is a wealthy, touristy coastal state capital in southern Brazil. Aggregator data shows restaurant prices there about 15% above the Brazilian average. Overall it is comparable to Porto Alegre and Curitiba, somewhat cheaper than prime areas of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, and more expensive than cities in northeastern Brazil.
